title: Why You Can't Stand Still With Your Eyes Closed
hook: Ever wondered why walking straight is easy, but standing still is hard?

narration.text: When you close your eyes, standing perfectly still becomes a real challenge.
This happens because your body uses a sense called proprioception.
It is your body's internal GPS, sensing where your limbs are without looking.
Proprioception works with your vision and inner ear for balance.
When you remove vision, proprioception and your inner ear work harder.
Your brain constantly makes tiny adjustments to keep you upright.
This amazing system keeps you steady, even when standing still feels wobbly.
Did you know your body had such a complex internal sense?

description: Discover the hidden sense that allows you to walk without looking at your feet, but makes standing still with closed eyes surprisingly difficult. Learn about proprioception and how it works with your vision and inner ear to maintain balance.
topic: Why you can walk a straight line but struggle to stand still with your eyes closed, explaining proprioception and balance.
